text: Corporations centralize power in order to pursue a singular strategy that efficiently exploits market circumstances, but this produces instability when the market swings, because a brittle hierarchy may crash before it can reorganize to handle a new challenge.
citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Preface to (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782191
abstract: Corporations tend to have centralized power, because they wish to employ a singu- lar strategy to efficiently exploit the circumstances of the market. However, this leads to instability whenever the market swings.
